Pure cosmetics: such string leads to a tree item with "App Type: MBIMUiccAppTypeUnknown" which seems redundant. 
Would it make sense to simplify it and display instead "App Type: Unknown" ? I think this is what I did initially in the MBIM dissector and it would ensure a global coherency (I wrote this dissector years ago so my memory could fail)
will fix it

Up to now, MBIM xas exclusively using UTF-16 encoding, not UTF-8. Did they change that? Are you sure you should not be using ENC_UTF_16 (was it tested with a capture)? The same applies for all the added strings in this change.
confirmed app_name and local_pin are UTF8. The others are bytes. Will fix them
will fix it

MBIM: dissect new UICC commands of MBIM extended version 1.0

Add support for the following CID:
MBIM_CID_MS_UICC_APP_LIST

I got your point now. I confirmed an uicc_app_info length is 296 and static. So I will fix it like below
`const gint max_app_elem_size = 296;`

Up to this point, we have consumed 288 bytes out of 296. Does it mean that:
- Pin Ref is up to 8 bytes
- padding is inserted if num_pins < 8
If there is no explicit padding, then you are not highlighting the right number of bytes in the subtree
It means Pin Ref is up to 8 bytes. And padding is inserted if num_pins < 8. A app_info length is 296 and static, so it should highlight the right number of bytes.
OK thanks for the clarification
